docs.title: Well Log Classifier
docs.text: Automated lithology classification from gamma, resistivity, neutron, density and sonic logs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "Well Log Classifier", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Source: Synthetic data generator (data_generator.py)
  • Samples: 5,000 well log records across 5 lithologies
  • Preprocessing: StandardScaler for numeric features, LabelEncoder for lithology labels
  • Features: gamma_ray, resistivity, neutron_porosity, density_porosity, sonic, caliper

docs.title: Lithology Classifier
docs.text:
• Algorithm: VotingClassifier (RandomForest + GradientBoosting)
  • Task: Multi-class classification (5 rock types)
  • Input: 6 well log features
  • Output: Lithology class + probability distribution
  • Serialization: pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Porosity Estimator
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoostingRegressor
  • Task: Regression (density porosity prediction)
  • Input: 6 well log features
  • Output: Porosity value (%)
  • Serialization: pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Raw well log values received via API
  2. Reshaped to (1, 6) feature array
  3. Label encoded (classification) or direct features (regression)
  4. Passed to trained model

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask
  • Port: 5008
  • Format: JSON request/response
  • Endpoints: 6 (classify, porosity, health, models, docs, index)

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML/CSS/JS (Jinja2 templates)
  • Charts: Plotly.js for probability visualization
  • Theme: Dark theme UI

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. User Input -> Dashboard form or API POST request
  2. Validation -> Check required fields and feature count
  3. Preprocessing -> Feature array construction
  4. Prediction -> Model inference (classification or regression)
  5. Post-processing -> Label decoding (classification), rounding
  6. Response -> JSON with predictions and probabilities

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.9-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN python train.py

EXPOSE 5008

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text:
docker build -t well-log-classifier .
docker run -p 5008:5008 well-log-classifier

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
  well-log-classifier:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "5008:5008"
    environment:
      - FLASK_ENV=production
    volumes:
      - model-data:/app/outputs

volumes:
  model-data:

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default FLASK_ENV Flask environment mode development PORT Server port 5008

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
• Use gunicorn for production serving: bash gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:5008 app:app
  • Set debug=False in app.py (already set)
  • Configure reverse proxy (nginx) for SSL termination
  • Set up health check monitoring on /api/health
  • Use a process manager (systemd, supervisor) for auto-restart

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
1. python train.py generates synthetic data and trains models
  2. Models are saved to outputs/models/
  3. python app.py loads models and starts the API server

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml): - Runs on push to main - Installs dependencies - Runs training pipeline - Executes API tests

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Well Log Classifier is a machine learning system for lithology classification and porosity estimation from well log measurements. It provides a web dashboard and REST API for real-time predictions.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cd well-log-classifier
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Train Models
docs.text:
python train.py

This generates 5,000 synthetic well log samples and trains: - Lithology Classifier (RandomForest + GradientBoosting ensemble) - Porosity Estimator (GradientBoosting)

Models are saved to outputs/models/.

docs.title: Run the Server
docs.text:
python app.py

Open http://localhost:5008 in your browser.

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• Lithology Classification Panel - Enter well log values and get rock type predictions with probability breakdown
  • Porosity Estimation Panel - Enter well log values and get density porosity predictions
  • Model Status - Shows loaded model types and feature columns
  • Results Visualization - Probability bar charts for lithology predictions

docs.title: Classify Lithology (curl)
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5008/api/classify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"features": [40, 50, 25, 22, 75, 8.5]}'

docs.title: Classify Lithology (Python)
docs.text:
import requests

response = requests.post("http://localhost:5008/api/classify", json={
    "features": [40, 50, 25, 22, 75, 8.5]
})
result = response.json()
print(f"Prediction: {result['prediction']}")
print(f"Probabilities: {result['probabilities']}")

docs.title: Estimate Porosity (curl)
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5008/api/porosity \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"features": [40, 50, 25, 22, 75, 8.5]}'

})

docs.text: Feature Description Typical Range gamma_ray Natural gamma radiation 10 - 200 API resistivity Electrical resistivity 5 - 300 ohm-m neutron_porosity Neutron porosity log 5 - 50 % density_porosity Density-derived porosity 5 - 40 % sonic Sonic travel time 40 - 100 us/ft caliper Borehole diameter 6 - 12 inches

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Models not loaded: Run python train.py before starting the server
  • Feature count error: Ensure exactly 6 features are provided in the correct order
  • Port in use: Change the port in app.py or stop other services on port 5008

Elaborado por Ing. Kelvin Cabrera

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
